evals.prompt: In our CloudApper UAT app a batch workflow updates child records, but the 'Process Item' workflow that should run on those updates never starts. In the workflow list the batch workflow is number 8 and Process Item is number 5. Both are on. What's wrong and how do I fix it?
evals.expected_output: Explains that a workflow's record changes only trigger workflows later in the list (higher Sequence), so the batch workflow must move before Process Item.
expectations: Says the cause is workflow order: changes only trigger workflows with a higher Sequence / later in the list
Recommends moving the batch workflow before Process Item
Mentions keeping the order the same in Production (or other environments)
Does not offer to run or trigger a workflow itself

evals.prompt: Some CloudApper records are stuck at Status = Running. I edited them and set Status to Running again so the processing workflow would pick them up, but nothing happened. The workflow triggers on Status _IsUpdated. Why?
evals.expected_output: The _IsUpdated trigger only fires on a real change; set an intermediate value such as Pending first, or route Pending/Running.
expectations: Says _IsUpdated only fires when the value actually changes
Suggests setting an intermediate value (e.g. Pending) first, or a route that picks Pending when the current value is Running

evals.prompt: My CloudApper backend workflow has a Router with two routes: 'Amount > 100' and 'Amount > 50'. For a record with Amount 150 both branches ran. Is this a platform bug?
evals.expected_output: Not a bug: a Router runs every route whose condition is true. Make conditions mutually exclusive and add an else route.
expectations: Says a Router runs every true route, not just the first
Recommends mutually exclusive conditions (e.g. 'Amount > 50 AND Amount <= 100')
Recommends an explicit else route

evals.prompt: In a CloudApper workflow I LOOKUP_RECORDS the rows of a period, then in a FOREACH I delete duplicates and update the others. The log shows 'No record found to update' for some items. What's going on?
evals.expected_output: The FOREACH iterates the list as fetched, so deleted records are still iterated. Delete first in one bulk step, then fetch and loop.
expectations: Explains that the loop still iterates records deleted inside it
Recommends deleting in one bulk step before fetching the list for the loop

evals.prompt: Design a nightly CloudApper workflow that syncs about 5,000 employees from a vendor REST API into an Employee form. Keep it short: the node chain and the key design decisions.
evals.expected_output: An upsert-based, batched sync with one token per run or batch, real failure handling and a sync log.
expectations: Uses an upsert (SAVE_RECORDS keyed on the external ID) rather than CREATE_RECORD
Gets one token per run or per batch, not per employee
Batches the calls or records instead of one call per employee
Handles failures beyond a '!= 200' route (timeouts or empty responses, error status, retry)
Writes a sync-log record per run (start, end, counts, errors) or equivalent
Keeps URLs, batch size or watermark in a settings/config record rather than hard-coded

evals.prompt: I want to see what happens to each item in my CloudApper FOREACH. Where should I put a DEBUG_LOG node?
evals.expected_output: Not inside the loop (it keeps one pass only); append to a text variable or counter in each pass and log once after the loop.
expectations: Advises against a DEBUG_LOG inside the FOREACH because it keeps only one pass
Suggests appending a line to a workflow variable (or a counter) in each pass and logging it once after the loop
Mentions resetting the variable at the start of the run

evals.prompt: I just started a CloudApper batch rerun that updates 24 records; the batch workflow finished in a few seconds. Can I start the next batch of 24 right away?
evals.expected_output: No: the triggered runs execute one at a time after the caller finished; starting another batch can lose triggered runs. Check the records' statuses first.
expectations: Says the triggered runs may still be queued and execute one at a time after the batch workflow finished
Advises waiting and checking the triggered records' statuses before starting the next batch
Warns that a second batch started meanwhile can lose its triggered runs

evals.prompt: In a CloudApper workflow, show the hours worked between Clock In and Clock Out as HH:MM. What expression should I use?
evals.expected_output: Use DateDiffMinute, round total minutes first, then split into hours and minutes; DateDiffHour truncates.
expectations: Uses DateDiffMinute (not DateDiffHour) for the calculation
Rounds the total minutes before splitting into hours and minutes, or otherwise avoids a ':60' result

evals.prompt: Please change the trigger of the 'Approve Timesheet' workflow in our CloudApper Production app from On Create to On Update.
evals.expected_output: Treats Production as read-only by default: confirms the environment and the specific change before doing anything, and suggests making and testing it in UAT first.
expectations: Does not make the change without first confirming the environment and this specific Production change
Suggests making or testing the change in UAT first
Mentions backing up the workflow before editing it

evals.prompt: Add this to the cloudapper skill: the Delay node seems to stop at 60 minutes even when set to 90. We saw it once in the Acme Foods UAT app, in the 'Acme Payroll Export' workflow.
evals.expected_output: Adds a generic entry directly to the right references/wp-*.md file with the next free WP number and status Hypothesis, without the customer or workflow names, adds its wp-index.md and CHANGELOG.md lines, runs check_skill.py and commits on local main.
expectations: Edits the matching references/wp-*.md file in the same session instead of writing a draft or asking for review
Uses the next free WP number (from references/wp-index.md) and the entry format (Rule, Why, Caveats, Status with Evidence)
Sets the status to Hypothesis
Leaves out 'Acme Foods' and 'Acme Payroll Export' (uses generic wording)
Adds the wp-index.md and CHANGELOG.md lines and runs scripts/check_skill.py
